# Planned scope

**Status:** planning outline. This project does not contain a completed Volume II
manuscript. Readers should first understand Volume I's question, design, data,
uncertainty, and reporting framework.

Volume II extends association into adjusted models and specialist analyses.
Confounding, predictor coding, interaction, model assumptions, and interpretation
must be connected to the study design. The volume should distinguish an explanatory
or association model from a prediction task.

| Planned chapter | Intended contribution |
|:----------------|:----------------------|
| 1. From association to modeling | Adjustment, confounding, effect modification, and analysis objectives |
| 2. Multiple linear regression | Conditional coefficients, coding, collinearity, diagnostics, and reporting |
| 3. Multiple logistic regression | Adjusted OR, reference groups, interactions, fit, and predicted probabilities |
| 4. Model assessment | Residuals, influence, model specification, and an introduction to validation |
| 5. Count data models | Poisson assumptions, person-time offsets, overdispersion, and negative binomial models |
| 6. Risk models | Difference and ratio scales; risk versus odds; supported modeling alternatives |
| 7. Survival analysis | Censoring, risk sets, Kaplan–Meier curves, and log-rank comparisons |
| 8. Cox regression | Conditional hazard ratios, proportional hazards, and adjusted survival models |
| 9. Diagnostic test evaluation | Sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, ROC, AUC, and context-dependent cut-offs |
| 10. Reliability and agreement | Internal consistency, kappa, ICC, and the distinction between reliability and agreement |
| 11. Factorial ANOVA | Main effects, interaction, planned contrasts, and conditional interpretation |
| 12. Repeated measures ANOVA | Within-person structure, sphericity, corrections, and missing observations |
| 13. Writing model results | Model definitions, tables, uncertainty, diagnostic findings, and limitations |
| 14. Applied modeling cases | Complete cohort and case-control workflows, with verified software output |

## Delivery requirements

Use the same chapter sequence and separate Hands-on note layout as Volume I.
Specify the installed jamovi and module versions for specialist procedures.
If a procedure requires an add-on or R, name the dependency and provide a tested
path; do not imply that all specialist analyses are available in the core menus.

Each adjusted example needs a stated target, defensible predictor selection,
coding and reference levels, missing-data handling, model assessment, and a
result that remains on the correct scale. Statistical adjustment alone does
not establish causal identification.

Model assessment in this volume concerns specification, fit, and basic diagnostic
judgments. Formal prediction development, resampling, calibration, transportability,
and external validation are developed in Volume III. Reliability coefficients
are introduced here; detailed method-comparison limits of agreement are developed
in Volume III. These boundaries prevent duplicate chapters with different claims.

Planned appendices include diagnostic checklists, model selection guidance,
reporting templates, and documented practice datasets. They are not supplied
as completed appendices in the current review project.
